output_list.reason: The mintToken function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The initial_supply parameter is provided by users, and the totalSupply is increased by this amount during minting. If initial_supply is sufficiently large, the totalSupply value will overflow, causing it to become very small, and allowing the owner to steal the funds of other users.

The transfer function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The balances[msg.sender] -= value; line can overflow if balances[msg.sender] is sufficiently large, allowing the balances of other users to become negative.

The transferFrom function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The balances[from] -= value; and allowed[from][msg.sender] -= value; lines can overflow if balances[from] or allowed[from][msg.sender] is sufficiently large, allowing the balances of other users to become negative.

The approve function has a wrong logic vulnerability. The _amount parameter is provided by users, and there is no check to ensure it is not set to a large value, allowing attackers to exploit this function to their advantage.

The transferFrom function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The balances[to] += value; line can overflow if balances[to] is sufficiently large, allowing the balances of other users to become negative.
